item.text: {"chapter_id":"6B","answers":[{"question_id":"6B.1","answer":"The government made welfare a substantive, though contested, policy purpose. It enacted Bürgergeld with higher benefits, inflation protection, training support and stated dignity objectives; expanded housing benefit; adopted a care reform; funded social protection and energy relief; and included social cohesion among budget priorities (BATCH-0026-E007; BATCH-0026-E008; BATCH-0032-E019; BATCH-0024-E008; BATCH-0027-E014; BATCH-0015-E009). Independent analysis found that energy-crisis transfers supported lower-income households and limited recession effects, although tax relief favored higher-income groups somewhat more (BATCH-0034-R12-E004; BATCH-0034-R12-E006). The commitment was not fully realized: child basic income remained disputed and underfunded, while poverty groups judged Bürgergeld inadequate and criticized sanctions and benefit design (BATCH-0005-E005; BATCH-0005-E006; BATCH-0019-E004; BATCH-0008-E012). Funding and legal sustainability were also weakened by the unconstitutional repurposing of €60 billion in COVID borrowing and the resulting cuts and uncertainty (BATCH-0021-E001; BATCH-0016-E016; BATCH-0024-E013). Attribution is primarily to the coalition and federal ministries rather than Scholz alone; many measures were continuations or future-dated, and 2023 outcomes are only partly observable.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0026-E008","BATCH-0032-E019","BATCH-0024-E008","BATCH-0027-E014","BATCH-0034-R12-E004","BATCH-0034-R12-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0005-E005","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0019-E004","BATCH-0008-E012","BATCH-0021-E001","BATCH-0016-E016","BATCH-0024-E013"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most evidence concerns federal policy design or modeled effects rather than verified service outcomes.","Scholz’s personal contribution is generally indirect through coalition leadership.","Housing, education quality, nutrition and long-term poverty effects are incompletely evidenced."]},{"question_id":"6B.2","answer":"Access improved in several domains through Bürgergeld, Wohngeld Plus, energy relief, broader asylum integration-course eligibility, refugee access to work, schools and universities, higher BAföG support, and care-law reforms (BATCH-0026-E007; BATCH-0024-E008; BATCH-0027-E007; BATCH-0011-R01-E006; BATCH-0020-E007; BATCH-0027-E014). DIW estimated that price relief and transfers reduced energy-shock damage and supported consumption, including among lower-income households (BATCH-0034-R12-E001; BATCH-0034-R12-E004). Actual access remained uneven: only about 30% of lower-income families received the child supplement, asylum reception was overcrowded, health and social assistance were harder to obtain, asylum counselling was underfunded, and municipal digital services lagged substantially (BATCH-0016-E011; BATCH-0011-R01-E005; BATCH-0011-R03-E011; BATCH-0029-E001). Housing construction approvals fell sharply, and the supplied evidence does not show that benefit expansion translated into broad affordability or quality gains (BATCH-0023-E001; BATCH-0023-E002). Policy attribution is federal and intergovernmental; many implementation responsibilities lay with Länder and municipalities, and several benefits were future-dated.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0024-E008","BATCH-0027-E007","BATCH-0011-R01-E006","BATCH-0020-E007","BATCH-0034-R12-E001","BATCH-0034-R12-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E011","BATCH-0011-R01-E005","BATCH-0011-R03-E011","BATCH-0029-E001","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0023-E002"],"limitations_and_gaps":["No complete executed-budget and uptake series spans all listed service domains.","Quality, affordability and regional incidence are better documented for asylum and housing than for ordinary health, education and sanitation services.","Some reported outcomes use 2022 baselines or future implementation dates."]},{"question_id":"6B.3","answer":"The government adopted several targeted protections: temporary protection and social access for roughly 1.1 million Ukrainians, expanded housing benefit and family-home loans, care benefits, disability-employment enforcement, hate-crime prevention, and increased support for care workers and vulnerable asylum applicants (BATCH-0008-E004; BATCH-0027-E003; BATCH-0027-E014; BATCH-0009-E019; BATCH-0008-E001; BATCH-0011-R03-E006). Energy transfers were modeled as relatively more beneficial to lower-income households, and child poverty risk fell from 15.0% to 14.0% in 2023, though large inequalities remained (BATCH-0034-R12-E004; BATCH-0024-E001; BATCH-0024-E002). Protection was incomplete and uneven: child poverty remained high, shelter capacity was deficient, asylum reception was overcrowded, vulnerable-person screening was not systematic, and the Afghan humanitarian programme admitted far fewer people than intended (BATCH-0020-E005; BATCH-0009-E017; BATCH-0011-R03-E002; BATCH-0011-R03-E013). Women, children, disabled people, minorities and migrants continued to face documented exclusion or violence, with implementation often controlled by Länder and municipalities rather than Scholz personally.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0027-E003","BATCH-0027-E014","BATCH-0009-E019","BATCH-0008-E001","BATCH-0034-R12-E004","BATCH-0024-E001"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0024-E002","BATCH-0020-E005","BATCH-0009-E017","BATCH-0011-R03-E002","BATCH-0011-R03-E013","BATCH-0011-R04-E014"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Evidence of poor regions, older people and rural service incidence is limited.","Child-poverty and violence indicators are population outcomes with uncertain policy attribution.","Many protective measures were enacted late in the period or had future-dated effects."]},{"question_id":"6B.4","answer":"There is evidence of professional administrative capacity in important areas: BAMF had 8,447 positions, quality controls, branch monitoring and 1,267 specialist officers for vulnerable applicants; asylum interpreters had training and impartiality standards; and care reform included staffing pools, qualification measures and digitalization support (BATCH-0011-R01-E010; BATCH-0011-R03-E006; BATCH-0011-R02-E001; BATCH-0033-E023). However, staffing and procurement failures undermined delivery. Auditors found insufficient staff to process funding applications, delayed programmes, inefficient administration and extreme procurement overpricing, while asylum counselling and local youth welfare suffered from inadequate staffing and expertise (BATCH-0003-E011; BATCH-0004-E009; BATCH-0003-E014; BATCH-0011-R03-E011; BATCH-0011-R03-E009). Transparent merit-based appointments and procurement are therefore mixed rather than established across the welfare portfolio. The findings concern ministries and agencies under Scholz’s government, but do not show his personal appointment or supervision of individual officials.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-R01-E010","BATCH-0011-R03-E006","BATCH-0011-R02-E001","BATCH-0033-E023"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E011","BATCH-0004-E009","BATCH-0003-E014","BATCH-0011-R03-E011","BATCH-0011-R03-E009"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Evidence is strongest for BAMF and weaker for health, education, housing and social-protection administrations.","The index rarely identifies appointment criteria, retention decisions or procurement competition in social-service agencies.","No comprehensive staffing-to-workload or service-quality evaluation is supplied."]},{"question_id":"6B.5","answer":"The government and agencies collected substantial welfare data and commissioned evaluations: BMAS funded representative studies on older people, disability participation and transfer incentives; Destatis published service and poverty statistics; BAMF used quality controls and branch monitoring; and hospital reform included transparency and continued evaluation (BATCH-0008-E024; BATCH-0008-E025; BATCH-0008-E027; BATCH-0011-R01-E010; BATCH-0025-E019). Courts and auditors also exposed failures, including unlawful surveillance, poor pension-subsidy transparency, weak programme administration, and budget illegality, followed by some corrections such as a supplementary budget, data-retention reform proposals and revised asylum information practices (BATCH-0003-E001; BATCH-0003-E009; BATCH-0016-E016; BATCH-0005-E008; BATCH-0011-R04-E003). The adverse evidence is that research-data infrastructure was inadequate, many programmes lacked outcome monitoring, and major commitments remained proposals or were not corrected promptly: child basic-income design stalled, digital-service targets were missed, and vulnerability guidance was not systematically monitored (BATCH-0009-E007; BATCH-0005-E006; BATCH-0009-E012; BATCH-0011-R03-E004). Thus measurement and judicial correction existed, but feedback into timely welfare redesign was inconsistent.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E024","BATCH-0008-E025","BATCH-0008-E027","BATCH-0011-R01-E010","BATCH-0025-E019","BATCH-0016-E016"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0009-E007","BATCH-0005-E006","BATCH-0009-E012","BATCH-0011-R03-E004","BATCH-0003-E001","BATCH-0003-E009"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The index often supplies study designs or audit titles without findings or evidence of implemented recommendations.","Independent evaluation of benefit adequacy, service quality and group incidence is incomplete.","Correction is frequently attributable to courts or ministries rather than a documented personal Scholz decision."]},{"question_id":"6B.6","answer":"Crisis response was a significant government activity. During the energy shock, Germany diversified supplies, filled storage, built LNG capacity and funded price relief; DIW found that the measures and a mild winter limited economic dislocation and supported lower-income consumption (BATCH-0016-E001; BATCH-0016-E018; BATCH-0034-R12-E001; BATCH-0034-R12-E004). The government also extended Ukrainian protection, provided accommodation, labour-market and education access, funded refugee support, responded to Slovenian floods, and adopted a national strategy covering civil protection, food security and pandemic prevention (BATCH-0008-E004; BATCH-0027-E007; BATCH-0032-E008; BATCH-0026-E002). Countervailing evidence shows overcrowded reception centres, inadequate sanitation and health access, delayed Afghan admissions, rising poverty risk and persistent unequal exposure to inflation and housing costs (BATCH-0011-R04-E014; BATCH-0011-R03-E013; BATCH-0023-E012; BATCH-0025-E016). The energy response was partly successful but costly and later destabilized by the unconstitutional budget transfer; many measures were responses to external shocks rather than wholly ruler-created outcomes (BATCH-0021-E001; BATCH-0023-E011).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0016-E001","BATCH-0016-E018","BATCH-0034-R12-E001","BATCH-0034-R12-E004","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0027-E007","BATCH-0032-E008","BATCH-0026-E002"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-R04-E014","BATCH-0011-R03-E013","BATCH-0023-E012","BATCH-0025-E016","BATCH-0021-E001","BATCH-0023-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Pandemic preparedness is mostly documented as a strategy commitment, not tested performance in 2023.","Disaster and refugee outcomes depend heavily on Länder, municipalities, donors and weather conditions.","Distributional effects of energy relief are partly modeled rather than observed."]},{"question_id":"6B.7","answer":"Formal rules provided meaningful safeguards against arbitrary allocation: Bürgergeld included cooperative plans, arbitration and hardship review; housing-benefit rules supplied transparent eligibility guidance; asylum procedures added independent counselling and appeal mechanisms; and courts reviewed unlawful detention, data searches and disproportionate state action (BATCH-0026-E008; BATCH-0022-E010; BATCH-0011-R01-E003; BATCH-0011-R05-E012; BATCH-0011-R01-E016). However, welfare and protection remained conditional and administratively coercive in important areas. Asylum benefits could be reduced, residence obligations affected benefits, employment access was delayed, payment-card proposals contemplated restricted cash use, and family reunification for subsidiary-protection beneficiaries remained discretionary and quota-limited (BATCH-0011-R04-E008; BATCH-0011-R04-E011; BATCH-0011-R04-E016; BATCH-0011-R04-E008; BATCH-0011-R06-E005). Political protest bans and racial profiling further qualify the broader non-punitive environment, although many were subnational actions not personally attributable to Scholz (BATCH-0008-E008; BATCH-0011-R04-E006). Judicial remedies existed but recurring unlawful detention and uneven counselling show that formal rights did not consistently prevent administrative punishment or exclusion.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E008","BATCH-0022-E010","BATCH-0011-R01-E003","BATCH-0011-R05-E012","BATCH-0011-R01-E016"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-R04-E008","BATCH-0011-R04-E011","BATCH-0011-R04-E016","BATCH-0011-R06-E005","BATCH-0008-E008","BATCH-0011-R04-E006"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The index provides little direct evidence of political loyalty tests in ordinary welfare, jobs or housing allocation.","Many coercive practices predated Scholz and were implemented by Länder or local authorities.","Appeal success, remedy speed and individual incidence are incompletely quantified."]},{"question_id":"6B.8","answer":"The government enacted or advanced several equal-rights measures: it ended discriminatory blood-donation exclusions, ratified the ILO Violence and Harassment Convention, strengthened disability-employment penalties, expanded integration-course eligibility, adopted police-recording requirements intended to address racial profiling, and proposed simplified legal gender recognition (BATCH-0001-E006; BATCH-0008-E011; BATCH-0009-E019; BATCH-0011-R01-E006; BATCH-0008-E003; BATCH-0008-E006). Energy transfers were modeled as more supportive of lower-income households, and courts supplied remedies against disproportionate searches and surveillance (BATCH-0034-R12-E004; BATCH-0024-E003; BATCH-0009-E014). Practical equality remained weak: anti-discrimination reform promised in the coalition agreement had not been advanced, accessibility was inconsistent, shelters lacked roughly 15,000 places, asylum health and counselling access varied, and marginalized groups experienced protest bans, racial profiling, hate crime and underreporting (BATCH-0008-E002; BATCH-0009-E017; BATCH-0011-R01-E009; BATCH-0003-E007; BATCH-0003-E006). The gender-recognition bill was not enacted in 2023 and faced unresolved child-protection and data-privacy objections (BATCH-0034-R04-E004; BATCH-0034-R04-E005).","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0001-E006","BATCH-0008-E011","BATCH-0009-E019","BATCH-0011-R01-E006","BATCH-0008-E003","BATCH-0034-R12-E004"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E002","BATCH-0009-E017","BATCH-0011-R01-E009","BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0003-E006","BATCH-0034-R04-E004","BATCH-0034-R04-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most reforms lack 2023 enforcement or remedy data.","National averages conceal sharp group, regional and institutional variation.","Some positive measures were proposals, while several adverse incidents were subnational and not directly attributable to Scholz."]},{"question_id":"6B.9","answer":"The period produced durable or potentially durable institutions: Bürgergeld created structured integration and arbitration mechanisms; the care reform created financing, staffing, digitalization and municipal-support mechanisms; BAMF maintained specialist staff and quality systems; hospital reform negotiations proposed quality-linked funding and transparency; and the national security strategy established cross-government prevention and resilience processes (BATCH-0026-E008; BATCH-0029-E006; BATCH-0011-R03-E006; BATCH-0025-E019; BATCH-0026-E001). Reliable statutory funding was only partly demonstrated: care financing was increased, migration counselling received €81.5 million and social expenditure reached about €1.249 trillion, but the budget crisis threatened climate and investment programmes and auditors warned of weak sustainability and opaque transfers (BATCH-0011-R06-E008; BATCH-0008-E026; BATCH-0003-E001; BATCH-0021-E001). Implementation and resilience were mixed: digital targets were missed, local service systems remained fragmented, Afghan and asylum programmes were delayed, and several institutions depended on future legislation or funding (BATCH-0009-E012; BATCH-0011-R04-E007; BATCH-0011-R03-E013). The evidence supports institution-building in selected sectors, not proof of a uniformly professional and durable welfare state beyond personal rule.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0026-E008","BATCH-0029-E006","BATCH-0011-R03-E006","BATCH-0025-E019","BATCH-0026-E001","BATCH-0011-R06-E008"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0008-E026","BATCH-0003-E001","BATCH-0021-E001","BATCH-0009-E012","BATCH-0011-R04-E007","BATCH-0011-R03-E013"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Long-term survival and performance beyond 2023 cannot yet be observed for many new institutions.","Professional staffing and transparent standards are well evidenced for BAMF but less so for general welfare administration.","The index does not establish completed implementation of several announced reforms."]},{"question_id":"6B.10","answer":"Ordinary people experienced some measurable, attributable improvements, but the end-period picture was mixed rather than broadly transformative. Child-poverty risk fell from 15.0% to 14.0%; BAföG recipients and average support increased; social transfers, energy relief and tax measures supported incomes and limited the recession; and lower-income wages rose strongly in 2023 (BATCH-0024-E001; BATCH-0020-E007; BATCH-0034-R12-E004; BATCH-0035-E007). The government also expanded access for Ukrainians, introduced Bürgergeld and Wohngeld Plus, and enacted care and disability measures (BATCH-0026-E007; BATCH-0024-E008; BATCH-0008-E004; BATCH-0027-E014). Against this, 17.7 million people remained at risk of poverty or social exclusion, 2.1 million children remained at poverty risk, lower-income households had suffered cumulative real-income losses, housing approvals collapsed, employment rose mainly through foreign workers while unemployment increased, and care, asylum, shelter and childcare capacity remained strained (BATCH-0023-E012; BATCH-0024-E002; BATCH-0025-E016; BATCH-0023-E001; BATCH-0009-E021; BATCH-0011-R04-E014; BATCH-0011-R06-E011). Attribution is constrained by the energy shock, war, monetary policy, inherited programmes, Länder and municipal delivery, and measurement lags; several apparent gains are modeled, provisional or not demonstrably durable.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0024-E001","BATCH-0020-E007","BATCH-0034-R12-E004","BATCH-0035-E007","BATCH-0026-E007","BATCH-0024-E008","BATCH-0008-E004","BATCH-0027-E014"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0023-E012","BATCH-0024-E002","BATCH-0025-E016","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0009-E021","BATCH-0011-R04-E014","BATCH-0011-R06-E011"],"limitations_and_gaps":["Most income indicators use prior-year income or provisional estimates and cannot isolate 2023 decisions.","Durability beyond the period is not established.","There is limited comparable evidence for water, sanitation, housing quality, regional inequality and disadvantaged-group life chances."]}],"cross_lens_observations":["The strongest evidence concerns federal social-transfer, energy-relief, refugee-protection, care and administrative reforms; evidence is weaker for broad service quality and durable outcomes.","Positive policy design and crisis mitigation coexist with substantial implementation failures, regional variation, poverty, housing constraints and unequal access.","Attribution generally rests with the Scholz-led coalition and federal institutions, while Länder, municipalities, courts, donors, private actors and external shocks materially shaped outcomes.","Formal monitoring, courts and audits provided correction mechanisms, but the record shows delayed or incomplete correction in several welfare and administrative programmes."]}
